exact_statement: For K>=0 and a coordinate product F=product_j h_j on n bits, let G differ from F on R vertices. For any nonempty proper factor subproduct h_J on m bits let r be its exact vertex distance to the class H<=KI. If all complete original m-bit cofactors of G are K-certified, then R>=2^(n-m)r. More generally at least max(0,2^(n-m)-floor(R/r)) cofactors violate K when r>0. With rho=r/2^m and mu=min_{dist(g,h_J)<r}(H(g)-KI(g))>0, the full signed terminal deficit is at least mu-(mu+Km)min(1,delta/rho), delta=R/2^n. A genuine least-essential-dimension positive K-witness on its n essential coordinates therefore has delta>=max_J rho_K(h_J) for every comparison product. For the three-bit point defect at K2 rho=1/8, sharp for the original one-factor-terminal criterion via the XOR edit family; repaired factor fibres do not imply all proper descendants are certified.
